title: Research: twisted helper exits do not make feedback cheaper through four registers
head: 80fea4aed2eacdca7ab4a3e2721e3dd1f355d344
body:
PR1868 asks whether allowing a twisted helper exit can make target feedback economical. This contribution answers every smallest instance through four total registers: for all 1,478 labeled `(h,y) -> (T h,y+K h)` endpoints, with arbitrary dirty inputs and any invertible T, the unrestricted XOR minimum equals the no-feedback minimum. This changes the restored-helper premise of PR1306; the larger three-helper/three-target question remains open.

The scoped package includes complete group BFS, independently coded literal truth-table BFS, attaining witnesses, exact source pins, six semantic controls and ten actual receipt-corruption rejections. Every XOR is priced; continuation absorption is not assumed free. No supplier, new kappa, selected-frontier change, or general no-feedback theorem is claimed.

Validation: the complete registered package passed with Python 3.12.14, including both relocated positive checks. `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-twisted-feedback-four-registers`. The prescribed PR1062 baseline passed after moving the Windows TEMP/TMP directories into writable workspace. Canonical main refreshed unchanged at `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4; the pre-submission overlap snapshot covers 688 open PRs. Full Discussion API coverage was rate limited; visible coordination pages were read with Curiosity Bot and the limitation is recorded.

Credit Sagar Thakrar / PR1868, @commdata2338 / PR1306, and the semantic-D/bit-word lineage named in the README. Prepared for ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human review or hosted CI success is claimed.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
